_schema_notes.purpose: Reference dataset of access-control (authentication/authorization) entry-point functions for Rust programs, the AC-finder counterpart to llm_api_functions.json. Used by find_ac_points to scan a RUPTA MIR dump for calls into known auth/authz crates so a reviewer can quickly enumerate every access-control decision point in a codebase.
_schema_notes.usage: find_ac_points matches MIR call sites against fn_name using the same three-strategy regex approach as find_llm_calls (direct / angle-bracket / short-name — see llm_api_finder.rs for the exact matching rules, reused verbatim by ac_finder.rs).
_schema_notes.match_rule: same textual match as llm_api_functions.json: direct path match, angle-bracket turbofish match, or last-two-segment short-name match against the MIR callee text
_schema_notes.verification_caveat: These signatures come from general knowledge of each crate's public API shape and have not been independently re-verified against current published docs (no context7/docs.rs lookup was performed when this file was authored). Spot-check against the target's actual installed crate version before trusting a match.
_schema_notes.kind_note: Optional per-entry field, defaults to "call" when absent. "attribute" marks a proc-macro attribute guard (e.g. actix-web-grants' #[has_permissions(...)]) rather than a function/method call -- find_ac_points_src is the only scanner that looks for these (via scan_attribute_guards, gated by crate reference like the method/short-name strategies); find_ac_points (MIR) and find_ac_points_llvm skip "attribute" entries entirely since the attribute expands away before codegen and leaves no realistic callee text to match.

jsonwebtoken.taint_role: primary JWT verification entry point (signature + claims validation); the actual access-control decision
reads the unverified header only (e.g. to pick a key id) — not itself a verification step, but commonly sits right before jsonwebtoken::decode

yup-oauth2.taint_role: Fetches an OAuth2 access token for a Google service account (via ServiceAccountAuthenticator::builder(key).build()), the yup-oauth2 analog of oauth2::Client::exchange_code above -- seen in the wild authenticating an app to Google Vertex AI/Cloud APIs. Same gated method-name matching as the rest of this catalogue; "token" is a common enough word that a false positive is possible on an unrelated .token(...) call in the same file, mitigated by the usual yup_oauth2 crate-reference gate.

axum-extractors.taint_role: custom axum auth extractor: apps that don't pull in axum-login/actix-identity/etc. almost always hand-roll their auth guard as `impl FromRequestParts<S> for MyAuthedUser`, decoding a bearer/JWT/session header inside `from_request_parts`. Matched as a trait-impl definition site (heuristically gated on an auth-flavored signal in the impl body, e.g. Authorization/Bearer/JWT/session/cookie/X-Forwarded-*), not a function call, since the pattern is a definition rather than an invocation.

`TypedHeader<Authorization<Bearer>>` / `TypedHeader<Authorization<Basic>>` handler-parameter extraction is axum's idiomatic way to pull a bearer/basic auth header out of a request; matched as a type-usage site rather than a call.

actix-web-extractors.taint_role: custom actix-web auth extractor: the actix-web analog to axum's FromRequestParts (see axum-extractors below). Apps that don't pull in a dedicated auth crate hand-roll their guard as `impl FromRequest for MyAuthedUser`, decoding a bearer/session header inside `from_request`. Matched as a trait-impl definition site (heuristically gated on an auth-flavored signal in the impl body -- same keyword table and code path as axum-extractors), not a function call.

custom-authz-module.taint_role: App-specific (bionic-gpt) but a common naming convention (an `authz` module's `get_permissions`) worth cataloging as a worked example: loads the caller's RBAC permission set for a team and, critically, also sets the Postgres `row_level_security.user_id` session variable that every RLS policy in the schema keys off (via the private `set_rls_and_encryption_keys` helper it calls internally). The source's own comment calls this out: 'Important, this does the IDOR for all requests with a team. Do not remove.' Caught by the existing generic direct/type-method matchers -- no scanner code changes needed, just a catalogue entry (see 'Adding a new library' in AC_FINDER.md).
Sic -- a real typo in bionic-gpt's own source (missing an 's'), not a mistake in this catalogue. Thin wrapper around get_permissions that resolves a public team id first.
Direct RLS user-id setter used by code paths (tool-runtime, background jobs) that establish per-user DB scoping without going through the full team-scoped get_permissions.

outbound-credential-header.taint_role: Attaches a credential to an outbound request when the header name is a known auth header (Authorization, x-api-key, api-key, x-goog-api-key, ...) -- the pattern an app uses to authenticate *itself* as a client to a downstream API (e.g. an LLM provider). See src/ac_hints.rs AUTH_HEADER_NAMES for the full table; find_ac_points_src only (a definite header-name match, not a call-shape catalogue entry).
reqwest's typed convenience method for attaching a Bearer credential; same outbound-authentication role as a manual Authorization header.
reqwest's typed convenience method for attaching HTTP Basic credentials.

The non-reqwest analog of RequestBuilder::header above: attaches a credential by inserting directly into a header map/HashMap when the header name is a known auth header, for HTTP clients built by hand instead of via reqwest's builder chain (e.g. opentelemetry-otlp's SpanExporter::builder().with_headers(map)). find_ac_points_src only, and additionally gated on the receiver identifier containing "header" (e.g. `headers.insert(...)`, `header_map.insert(...)`) on top of the header-name match, since plain `.insert(` is far too generic a method name (HashMap/BTreeMap/Vec/DB rows/...) to gate on the string literal alone the way `.header(` can.

The URL-query-string sibling of RequestBuilder::header above: attaches a credential as a `?key=...`/`?access_token=...` query parameter instead of a header -- the pattern the Gemini Developer API (and some other vendor-less-SDK REST APIs) uses. See src/ac_hints.rs AUTH_QUERY_PARAM_NAMES for the full table and its higher false-positive-risk note ("key" alone is a much more generic word than anything in AUTH_HEADER_NAMES). find_ac_points_src only, and scans the whole `.query(...)` call's argument list (commonly a param list/map carrying several params at once) rather than one string per call the way `.header(...)` is.

inbound-credential-header.taint_role: The inbound analog of outbound-credential-header: reads a credential directly out of an *incoming* request's header map (axum's `Parts::headers` / `HeaderMap`, actix-web's `HttpRequest::headers()`) via a hand-rolled `.get("Authorization")`/`.get("x-api-key")` check, rather than a structured extractor (`impl FromRequestParts`, `TypedHeader<Authorization<Bearer>>`) -- e.g. bionic-gpt's crates/web-server/handlers/api_pipeline.rs, which checks a Bearer API key pulled from `headers.get("Authorization")` against the database. find_ac_points_src only, and additionally gated on the receiver identifier containing "header" (e.g. `headers.get(...)`, `parts.headers.get(...)`) or the `.headers().get(...)` method-call chain (actix-web's `HttpRequest::headers()`), on top of the header-name match, since plain `.get(` is far too generic a method name (HashMap/Option/Vec/...) to gate on the string literal alone the way `.header(` can.

raw-http-authz.taint_role: catch-all for calls to an external authn/authz service (OAuth2/OIDC provider, OPA, Vault, Keycloak) made without an SDK; ac_hint narrows this using nearby string literals via ac_hints.rs
blocking counterpart to reqwest::RequestBuilder::send; same catch-all role
